name: Moore-Federman Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Moore-Federman Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of multiple symmetric, non-encapsulated lipomatous masses predominantly in the neck, upper trunk, and proximal limbs
Peripheral neuropathy or muscle weakness associated with the syndrome
Positive family history of similar lipomatous lesions

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of symmetric lipomatosis with or without neurological involvement; supportive criteria such as alcohol use or family history strengthen diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; imaging and biopsy may assist in excluding malignancy

laboratory: Elevated liver enzymes in patients with alcohol use
Normal lipid profile despite fat accumulation
imaging: MRI or CT showing symmetric, diffuse, non-encapsulated fat deposits
Nerve conduction studies indicating peripheral neuropathy
genetic: No definitive genetic mutation identified; possible mitochondrial DNA involvement
other: Histopathology showing mature adipose tissue without encapsulation
Clinical history of chronic alcohol use

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly affects lower limbs with sparing of feet
Lack of association with alcohol use

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of lipomatous masses suggesting malignancy
Onset of severe neuropathic pain or motor deficits
Signs of airway obstruction due to neck mass
